context:
Goal: a merge that checks what is unproven and does not repeat what CI already proved.
Problem (rule): decision lanes-run-no-full-ci-job (your item 27 a, 2026-10-27) says the batch runner runs lane lint on each lane head before the join and refuses a red lane. Lane lint took about 17 min in one lane's run (your paste 20:36; one sample). If the head's all-jobs-passed check is green, the full run already ran lint, so lane lint may repeat work. Changing it changes a ruling, so it needs your word.
Based on (read): the ruling text above, read by triage; the consultant's audit, unchecked by triage.
Departs from: main — the merge runs lane lint every time; this makes it skip when the head's all-jobs-passed check is green.
Meanwhile: lane lint runs as it does today.
lastAnswer: a: skip lane lint at the merge when the head's all-jobs-passed rollup is green (owner 21:01 CST via the consultant)

options.gain: Each merge saves the lint run when CI already ran it.
options.label: Skip lane lint at the merge when the head's all-jobs-passed check is green (recommended by the consultant)
options.lose: A green all-jobs-passed check that did not run lint would let a lint red through; the audit has not shown that case.

options.gain: No change to a ruling you made.
options.label: Keep lane lint at every merge
options.lose: The same lint runs twice on every PR.

owner: consultant (session_013NEJKz5AWFJhGvmCUoi6wQ), from its merge-tool audit; posted by triage (session_013NEJKzCzoWhfP8FMCPtQU6)
reply: Filed. The merge skips lane lint on a green rollup, and the lane merge-tool-audit-fixes rewrites the decision line. It is a change to your 2026-10-27 ruling, so the ruling record says so.
short: Skip lane lint at the merge when the head's all-jobs-passed check is green?
title: Should the merge skip its lane lint when the head's all-jobs-passed check is already green?
why: Your 2026-10-27 ruling (item 27 a) makes the batch runner run lane lint again before the join; with a full CI run now green, that second lint may only repeat it, and your word is needed to change a ruling.
